body: Pasikuda Beach - A Hidden Gem on Sri Lanka's East CoastPasikuda Beach is one of Sri Lanka's most pristine and tranquil coastal destinations, located on the eastern shoreline in the Batticaloa District. Known for its shallow, calm waters and powder-soft golden sand, this beach offers a perfect blend of relaxation and natural beauty that rivals any tropical paradise.Why Visit Pasikuda BeachCrystal Clear Waters & Safe SwimmingPasikuda is famous for having one of the longest stretches of shallow reef in the world. The calm, turquoise waters extend up to 150-200 meters from shore at a consistent shallow depth, making it incredibly safe for families with children and non-swimmers. The gentle waves and absence of strong currents create an ideal environment for leisurely swimming and wading.Pristine Natural BeautyThe beach boasts a stunning crescent-shaped bay with soft, golden sand that stretches for kilometers. The water is remarkably clear, allowing you to see fish swimming around your feet. The sunrise views here are absolutely spectacular, painting the sky in vibrant oranges and pinks as the sun emerges over the Indian Ocean.Water Sports & ActivitiesSnorkeling and diving in the nearby coral reefsKayaking and stand-up paddleboardingJet skiing and banana boat ridesBeach volleyballBoat trips to nearby islands and lagoonsPeaceful AtmosphereUnlike some of Sri Lanka's more crowded western beaches, Pasikuda maintains a serene, uncrowded atmosphere. It's the perfect destination for those seeking relaxation away from the hustle and bustle.Best Time to VisitThe ideal time to visit Pasikuda Beach is from April to September when the east coast experiences dry, sunny weather. During these months, the sea is calm, the skies are clear, and rainfall is minimal. The west coast monsoon season makes the east coast the perfect alternative destination during this period.
title: Pasikuda Beach

body: If you’re looking for a beach getaway with crystal-clear waters, golden sands, and absolute tranquility, Pasikuda Beach is the perfect destination! Located on Sri Lanka’s east coast, this breathtaking bay is known for its calm, shallow waters, making it ideal for swimming, relaxing, and enjoying stunning sunsets.A Beach Like No Other 🏖️The best part about Pasikuda is the gentle, shallow waters—you can walk several meters into the sea, and the water remains at waist level! The waves are almost non-existent, making it one of the safest beaches in Sri Lanka, especially for families and kids.Water Activities & Fun 🏄‍♂️If you love water sports, Pasikuda has plenty to offer:✔️ Snorkeling & Diving – The coral reefs here are home to beautiful marine life.✔️ Jet Skiing & Kayaking – A thrilling way to explore the coastline.✔️ Boat Rides & Fishing – Perfect for a relaxing day at sea.Resorts & Food 🍽️Pasikuda is lined with luxury resorts like Uga Bay, Maalu Maalu, and Amaya Beach, offering direct beach access and stunning sea views. The food scene is fantastic too—if you love fresh seafood, you’ll find delicious crab, prawns, and traditional Sri Lankan rice & curry at the beachfront restaurants.Sunset Magic & Best Time to Visit 🌅Sunsets at Pasikuda are magical, with the sky painting the sea in shades of orange and pink. The best time to visit is from May to September, when the sea is at its calmest and the weather is perfect for beachside relaxation.Why You Should Visit 💙✔️ One of the most beautiful & safest beaches in Sri Lanka✔️ Perfect for relaxation, water sports, and stunning views✔️ Less crowded than southern beaches like Mirissa & UnawatunaPasikuda is truly a hidden gem for anyone looking for a peaceful and breathtaking beach escape. Whether you want to swim, enjoy luxury resorts, or simply unwind on the soft sands, this place will leave you with unforgettable memories.🌟 Would I visit again? Absolutely, without a doubt!
title: A Slice of Paradise – Pasikuda Beach 🌊🏝️

body: During clam season (March to October) the Pasikuda beach, with its white soft sand and its crystal clear shallow waters. Making it perfect for families to swim, with other activities like snorkeling and kayaking.After the Sri Lankan civil war ended in 2009 Pasikuda beach has become the most popular beach on the east coast and a favorite tourist location.We visited the beach during December which is when the waters are the roughest (November to February) making it more ideal for swimming or other activities. We were staying at Uga Bay resort so the beach was only meters away from our room. Even though the sea was very rough you can still walk along the beach and enjoy the magnificent view.We highly recommended coming to visit the Pasikudah beach during the calm season (March to October) and even staying at one of the Beach resorts (Uga Bay and etc) making it only a waking distance from your room and the resorts supplying equipment like kayaks.

Nearby there is a reef where a turtle lives, visibility under water is good (not the Maldives) but everything is visible (there are living corals). For those who like to snorkel, there is an option to go to Trincomalee on Pigeon Island. This is just a bomb, I have never seen anything better underwater, the corals are all alive, a lot of fish, turtles, reef sharks. There are no tourist trips there, because it is a nature reserve. Unfortunately only the areas outside the numerous hotels are swept for litter - outside of these areas there is the usual detritus at the high water line. Water sports are available, but do not dominate the area, so it is easy to find a quiet, peaceful place to chill out. No beach bars or cafes, just the hotels. No salespeople to annoy you, and very few flies to bother you. Heaven.

body: After visiting too many beaches polluted with unbelievable washed up plastics of all descriptions as well as rotting nylon fishing nets, Pasikudah beach comes as a golden tropical delight. Twice I walked the entire length of the beach ( a good hour and a half each way) and in the entire walk saw only TWO small pieces of plastic: a tiny bag and a child's small doll. AMAZING. Even where the fishing village fronts the beach, it is CLEAN. No garbage, no plastic, no rotting nets and absolutely no household trash dumped on the sands; just pristinely clean white coral sands.Here's why; the first resort owners to build there, the beach bungalow style Maalu Maalu invested largely on contemporary education for the local fishing village. Maalu Maalu also purchases the catch. The got together with them and relocated the entire village to the north of the beach, built two school rooms for the kids and pay the teaching fees for both the computer centre and language centre. They taught the fishermen to STOP fishing with dynamite (yes, dynamite) and also that it's imperative to create a pristine beach for their income and for future work for the kids; its all working. It's a paradise.On the beach, LSR , Lanka Sportsreizen provide water skiing, jet skiing, snorkel etc at very competitive price . Fun in the sun :) It was such a pleasure staying at Maalu Maalu Resort: excellent catch of the day seafood bar etc and easy beach access to the neighbouring resorts if you like to explore various menus. Having a fabulously CLEAN beach to enjoy and for endless strolls and bathing, sun, fun, white sands and turquoise tropical water.100% Bliss NB. In 6 weeks we were driven over 4,000 KLM's to many luxurious destinations: Pasikudah Beach was the only pristine tropical beach we landed on, and for small, quiet unobtrusive accommodation, Maalu Maalu is tops.
title: Pristine Golden Sands

body: This is a lovely looking beach although no real character - just big resort hotels. The sea is painful to walk into as there are huge quantities of sharp coral which you can't avoid. I spoke to local business owners whilst there and discovered that in 2009, the big hotels got together and destroyed the coral reefs in order to get rid of the waves created. The local businesses fought against this but there was nothing they could do. If you walk along the beach you will see piles and piles of dead coral - quite distressing. There is a Swiss NGO working to replant the coral and if you want to learn more, go chat to the manager Siva of Hotel Vasuki - a lovely man who is trying to improve the area and incidentally serves up an absolutely amazing curry and rice.
title: Beautiful looking beach, but at what cost!

body: It was not my first time to visit Pasikudah, When I was a kid I used to go with my family at least 2 times per year. But 2004 Tsunami stroked this beautiful bay so badly. Since the end of civil the war 2009 this place has become a popular tourist destination in eastern part of Sri Lanka. Mostly famous among the locals though recently there are number of forefingers visiting this beach. After the Tsunami it was my second visit with family and friends. Pasikudah is a calm wave-less and very low current clear water brighter sand beach so really suitable for children and people don't know how to swim. A 40 minutes drive from Batticaloa town. There are guards deployed to monitor the accidents. It was impressing to see all the star class accommodations and private beaches all over there. The officials must take more cautions about garbage and sanitary management. Nice to visit with family.

body: No waves but a calm beach, make sure you stay at a hotel such as maalu maalu resort or uga bay resort,so that you get a private beach and not the public beach where it would get overcrowded specially on weekends, try to go snorkeling if you do have the time. It costs around 3000rs for the glass bottom boat ride. The ride would be around 1km from the shore. You can pretty much jump off and do some snorkeling which would cost you around 500rs. Try going in the morning at around 7:00 am when the water is very calm and crystal clear. Good reefs with colorful fishes. And try waking up early morning to see the sunrise!! Breathtaking view from the shore!!
title: Pretty nice calm beach

body: If you are travelling to sri lanka or you are a citizen in island nation this is a must go beach. Bit isolated from the nearest town gives a serene calmness to the beach. The beach is surrounded by the super luxury hotels but you can always find a budget hotels in few hundred metes reach. Few food stalls are close to the beach but nothing much to eat.
title: Never miss

body: Greater place for morning and evening bath and swim. Super up waves, hotels near by, small shops. If you travel on week days, none other than Sri Lankan holidays then you can enjoy the beauty with lesser crowd. Otherwise, you will have to manage the domestic tourists as well. Since the civil war ended up recently, there are so many Sri Lankans visit here. Although, you may experienced with garbage dumped here and there on your way, the beach is beautiful.
title: Ideal place for Sea bath and enjoyable day

body: Passikudah is known for its nice sandy beach as well as for shallow calm water as a result of the bay there is a nice plot for general public in the middle of the resorts which recently came about highly recommended for beach lovers to take dip in this beautiful landscape
title: Excellent Place for Beach lovers

body: Passikudah Beach gained rapid popularity soon after the civil war ended. As soon as the first major hotels arrived so did the masses. It is not only popular among the wealthy seeking a beachside escapade but the common citizenry thronging in vans and trishaws especially during the long weekends and holidays. The public beach is but a small strip that resembles a large bathtub where everyone jumps in! On the average day this is all yours so do not despair!The nicer hotels hold some of the best beach frontage. Rightfully as one spending the big buck would expect, it is cordoned off using a psychological barrier effect and this allows you to enjoy at leisure as opposed to a rampage in water!Enjoy with responsibility and continue to keep the beach cleaner. This is a beach certainly worth the visit!
title: Pristine

body: We were there on a long weekend and the crowds were overwhelming. Can't say how it would be on a normal day.
title: Just too crowded

body: Had a evening bath and swim for about two hrs. Beach area need some cleaning. garbage is lying on top of the beach. no proper seating for people who do not step in to the water but have to wait for others to come back from sea.
title: visit with our friends

body: I visited Pasikuda beach recently, it was a Sunday and the beach was quite busy, there are no facilities for sitting other than on the sand, if you try to go onto hotel grounds which are NOT MARKED you are approached by security men and then by staff from the hotels who want to charge 500rupees for a beach bed with mattress for one hour use. The beach itself is excellent, you can walk for miles.
title: Great beach with poor facilities

body: Pasikuda beach is very beautiful and provides a superb location to see the sunrise. You need to be at the beach by 6am to see it. The ocean is not deep for few meters and is safe for an enjoyable family trip. The waves are not rough letting you relax and enjoy your time.
title: Safe beach and quite amazing

body: This is located in the Eastern coast of Sri Lanka. On your way or back to/from Batticaloa. This beach ids really beautiful and ideal place for swimming. There are hotels nearby but fully packed always.
